body.heading: Why rules ruin journals
paragraphs: Many journals die of good intentions: write every day, fill a page, be insightful, keep it forever. Each rule is another way to fail, and within a fortnight the notebook becomes a small monument to guilt.

The alternative is a journal with no rules at all. Write when there is something to offload or explore. Three lines or three pages. Legible or not. The journal serves you; you do not serve the journal.

body.heading: What to write when you do
paragraphs: Whatever is loudest: the thing you keep rehearsing, the decision going in circles, the good moment you want to keep. Writing slows thought to handwriting speed, which is often slow enough to finally hear it properly.
Keep it private — genuinely private, somewhere others will not read. Honesty on the page depends on it, and honesty is the entire point.

takeaway: No schedule, no standards, no audience: just write when it helps.
